title: SREV-159 PipeServer Thread Vector Lifetime
contracts: PipeServer owns a thread handle vector allocated from GetProcessHeap
Start must not create the server port or index m_Threads when the vector allocation failed
m_ThreadCount is the number of valid thread handles currently stored at the front of m_Threads
waits termination close and cleanup may operate only on m_ThreadCount valid handles
every successful CreateThread handle is eventually closed with CloseHandle
startup failure after partial thread creation shuts down the published port wakes existing worker threads closes their handles preserves the CreateThread GetLastError value and returns false
the HeapAlloc vector is freed with HeapFree in the destructor
does not change LPC message framing request dispatch target registration impersonation or server-port security descriptor policy
Linux source gate is not Windows runtime proof
runtime_gates: Windows SbieSvc build for PipeServer.h and PipeServer.cpp
forced HeapAlloc failure proves Start returns ERROR_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY before publishing the port
forced mid-loop CreateThread failure proves already-created workers exit and handles are closed
ordinary startup and shutdown smoke proves all worker handles close and normal LPC requests still dispatch
